summary_md: **Natural Language Processing Papers ([@HEI](https://x.com/HEI/status/2116669091674992856))** shares *Is Token Confidence Just Chain Length?* by Pragna Mallappa ([arXiv 2610.36709](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36709)), which audits sliding-window token-confidence pruning of reasoning chains with signal-processing tools to test whether it mostly tracks chain length.

referenced_urls.title: Is Token Confidence Just Chain Length? A Signal-Processing Audit...

media.description: Abstract of the paper auditing token-confidence chain filtering with signal processing, finding the windowed-minimum score mostly measures chain length.
media.ocr_text: Reasoning language models answer math problems by writing long chains of thought, and sampling many chains per problem and taking a majority vote raises accuracy at a large cost in generated text. A popular way to cut that cost scores each chain by the model's confidence in each token it writes, where a token is a word or part of a word. The method averages this confidence over a sliding window of 2048 tokens and keeps or stops chains based on the lowest average. We treat the confidence, recorded token by token, as a signal in the sense of audio or radio, and examine the method with standard signal-processing tools such as spectral analysis and statistical tests for detecting a sudden change. We sampled 16 chains for each of 500 problems from two math benchmarks with a small open reasoning model. The windowed-minimum score turns out to measure mostly how long a chain is.
